title: Machine learning derives a five-protein plasma classifier of COVID-19 mortality
summary: Using plasma proteomics, an XGBoost model trained on 88 discovery admission samples with 5-fold cross-validation selected a five-protein classifier (CRP, ECM1, IGFALS, HECW1, LCAT) for 28-day mortality. It reached AUC 0.88 in the discovery group and 0.80 in an independent 97-patient cohort from a second hospital, better than the 4C mortality and E-CURB65 scores. Cohorts are small (277 discovery, 97 validation), from a single country, and the result is prognostic rather than causal.
ai_technology: XGBoost trained on plasma proteomics with 5-fold cross-validation to select a mortality classifier
organization: Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Classifier performance was checked on an independent patient cohort from a second hospital.
evidence.unknown: Generalization beyond these cohorts and any clinical benefit were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Selected the protein panel and produced the mortality prediction model.
